# Papatūānuku, translated into industries: what the archetype actually does
The myths did not retire. They moved offices. This is the file on where **Papatūānuku** works now.

Papatūānuku's central myth is the separation of earth and sky, one of the most widely distributed creation narratives in Polynesia. The Māori version is preserved in nineteenth-century written versions of oral tradition collected by Grey, Best, and Smith.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **4 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.
## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Papatūānuku
- **Pantheon:** Polynesian
- **Domain of influence:** Earth, Creation, Fertility
- **Pattern seats:** 4
- **Sectors touched:** Energy & Natural World · Commerce & Governance · Home & Lifestyle
- **Strongest seat:** Agriculture, Food & Harvest
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 188 of 271
## The Myth at Work

**The Separation of Rangi and Papa.** In the beginning Ranginui, the Sky, and Papatūānuku, the Earth, clung together in a close embrace.  Their children — Tāne, Tāwhirimātea, Tangaroa, Tū, Rongo, and Haumia-tiketike — were born into the cramped darkness between their parents' bodies. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

**The Children of Papatūānuku.** Each of Papatūānuku's children claimed a domain from her body.  Tāne became lord of forests and birds. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.
## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest

*Farming, grain, food production, and agtech. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*The earth mother from whom all food comes.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Environmental & Climate Services

*Climate science, ecology, and sustainability consulting. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The land that gives birth to all living things; stewardship personified.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Ancestry & Heritage Services

*Genealogy, heritage research, and DNA ancestry. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

*Mother of the gods and of humankind; whakapapa recites every lineage in Aotearoa in layers back to her.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Papatūānuku performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Home, Hearth & Real Estate

*Property, home goods, and domestic services. (Sector: Home & Lifestyle)*

*The land that gives birth to all; in Aotearoa land is kin and the first address, not a commodity — her body under every title deed.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Papatūānuku performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

Read the myth again after the seats and it stops sounding ancient: Papatūānuku's central myth is the separation of earth and sky, one of the most widely distributed creation narratives in Polynesia. The age changed. The work did not.
## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity's documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The full derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.
## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in agriculture, food & harvest, environmental & climate services, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/papatuanuku/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit. The story is the pitch; the seats are just where it already works.
